Yuba River

Sadie Gill, Mark Tompkins

July 2020

Future Data Improvements

Instream Spawning and Rearing Habitat

Chinook

Data Source: Updated spawning, in-channel rearing, and floodplain rearing were provided directly by Morgan Neal (HDR, Inc.) as part of an analysis to account for projected suitable habitat created by Health Rivers and Landscapes (HRL) projects. These data were provided in an excel format stored in data-raw/watershed/yuba/data/HydraulicHabFlow_LYR_7-15-2024.xlsx.

Water depths and water velocities in the lower Yuba River were simulated by using a TUFLOW HPC 2D hydrodynamic model of the lower Yuba River using a 2017 digital elevation model (DEM). The 2017 DEM was developed subsequent to high flows that occurred during Winter of 2017 using Airborne Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), boat-based multibeam and single beam echosounding, and ground-based topographic surveying with Real-time kinematic (RTK) Global Positioning System (GPS) and robotic total stationing. The 2D model was run with a 3’x3’ computation mesh for flows <= 30,000 cfs and a 10’x10’ mesh for flows > 30,000 to 110,400 cfs. Detailed discussion of the calibration, validation and deployment of the 2017 2D model of the lower Yuba River is provided in Pasternack (in prep) and the documentation of the methodologies employed to produce the 2017 DEM is provided in Silva and Pasternack (2018).

Rearing hydraulic criteria:

  • Depth >= 0.5 and <= 4.0 ft
  • Velocity <= 3.0 ft/sec

Spawning hydraulic criteria:

  • Depth >= 1.0 and <= 2.5 ft
  • Velocity >= 1.0 and <= 4.0 ft/sec

Spawning substrate criteria and data:

  • Dominant substrate 2-10 cm
  • Mean diameter substrate data based on 2010-2011 and 2018-2020 surveys within the bankfull channel (5,000 cfs extent)

Existing condition in-channel and floodplain rearing habitat:

  • Delineation of in-channel and floodplain based on 1,5000 cfs wetted extent below DPD (as modified by HAllwood As-Built condition) and 1,750 cfs wetted extent above DPD
  • Based on preliminary YWA analysis of flow that meets the intent of Meaningful Floodplain Event (MFE) criteria during 80% of years using modeled daily hydrology below DPD and below Deer Creek.

Steelhead

Data Source: Spawning FWS 2010 (pgs 59-61) and Rearing FWS 2010 (pgs 74-76)

The instream spawning and rearing habitat for Steelhead in the Yuba River are based on data from the Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) flow-habitat relationship final reports. A 2-dimensional hydraulic and habitat model called River2D was used to model available spawning and rearing habitat. The FWS instream spawning and rearing data were provided by Mark Gard from the California Department of Fish and Wildlife in a spreadsheet. Mark Gard instructed us to use cells A4:H33 and A39:H68 of the ‘Yuba’ tab within the spreadsheet, representing the Englebright to Daguerre Segment (12.7 miles) and the Daguerre to Feather Segment (11.4 miles), respectively. For adult Steelhead, Mark Gard instructed us to use cells A73:B100 of the ‘Yuba’ tab within the spreadsheet.

Spawning WUA

The following plot shows the weighted usable spawning area (WUA) in square feet per thousand feet for Fall Run Chinook Salmon, Spring Run Chinook Salmon, and Steelhead. These area per length rates are multiplied by the total spawning reach length mapped by the Science Integration Team (SIT) to estimate available habitat.

Rearing WUA

The following plot shows the rearing WUA in square feet per thousand feet for Fall Run Chinook Salmon and Steelhead fry and juvenile. These rates are multiplied by the total rearing reach length mapped by the SIT to estimate available habitat.

Floodplain Rearing Habitat

Steelhead and Spring run

Data Source: SRH-2D hydraulic model developed by Dr. Greg Pasternack at the University of California, Davis

The entire mapped rearing extent of 23.1 miles was modeled using SRH-2D hydraulic model developed by Dr. Greg Pasternack at the University of California, Davis. An active channel area of 446.2 acres, estimated through remote sensing analysis, was subtracted from total inundated area to obtain inundated floodplain area.
